title: Adaptive speculative-decode router with acceptance calibration and staged rollback playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: Implement a production-ready speculative decoding router that chooses candidate models/kernels for a two-stage prefill->decode flow, continuously calibrates an acceptance metric, and provides deterministic fallback/rollback behavior under degraded conditions. Scope: runtime routing logic (router service + lightweight prober), acceptance metric design, telemetry/SLIs, staged rollout plan, and operational runbook. Out of scope: model fine-tuning for acceptance (handled by ModelOps) and heavy-weight data-plane rearchitecting.
background: We want to reduce p95/p99 latency and unit token cost by routing fast, approximate decoders on the optimistic path and committing to full decoders only when an acceptance metric indicates high confidence. Prior prototypes showed 10-18% cost reduction at comparable output quality, but lacked a robust acceptance calibration and clear rollback semantics for production incidents.
design_decisions: Acceptance metric will be a composite score: (normalized next-token logprob delta) + (top-k overlap with slow decoder surrogate) + (logit stability heuristic). Each submetric is z-scored per-model and combined with tunable weights.

Router uses kernel fingerprint + model signature to map requests to candidate stacks (fast-quantized decoder on GPU-opt, slow-reference decoder on high-accuracy kernels). Kernel affinity is preserved to maintain KV cache compatibility.
Prefill probe: small sample of tokens from prefill are decoded by both fast and slow stacks to compute an initial acceptance score without committing to full decode execution on slow path.

Two-tier fallback: (1) soft-commit: let optimistic decode continue but re-evaluate at N tokens; (2) hard-rollback: abort optimistic output and re-decode on slow path if acceptance < threshold after probe window.
Default thresholds: acceptance_accept >= 0.85 for immediate commit; probation window of 3 tokens with relaxed threshold 0.7 for soft-commit. Thresholds are configurable per-customer and per-model.
Operational default fallback model variants: degrade to a smaller exact decoder (higher memory protection) before falling back to CPU-hosted slow-reference in extreme cases.
Feature flags gate rollout: router-v1 (probing + thresholds) -> router-v1.1 (auto-calibration) -> router-v2 (traffic-aware kernel selection).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (instrumentation): add probe hooks to prefill path, expose candidate kernel fingerprints, and emit acceptance raw signals to telemetry. (owner: Arjun)
Phase 2 (router service): implement routing decision graph with pluggable acceptance calculators and kernel affinity checks. Add unit tests and deterministic sim harness. (owner: Katerina)
Phase 3 (canary): enable on 5% internal traffic with feature flag; collect acceptance distributions, false accept/false reject rates, latency delta, and cost delta. (owner: Maya)

Phase 4 (auto-calibration): implement rolling-window calibration that nudges weights and thresholds based on observed downstream QA and accept/reject outcomes. Keep a human-approved rollback threshold. (owner: Research)
Phase 5 (gradual rollout): 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with SLO gates. (owner: EngOps)
PR checklist: design doc link, integration tests, perf regression <2% p50; perf improvement target p95 -10% or cost/unit -8%.
acceptance_criteria: Router can be enabled behind a feature flag and toggled per-tenant.
Observed acceptance false-reject rate <= 1% and false-accept rate <= 2% on internal benchmark dataset (N=50k prompts).
No regression in correctness as measured by downstream eval prompts (semantic metrics within ±1% of baseline slow decoder).
p95 latency for optimistic path under production tail load must remain <= baseline p95 + 20ms and overall token cost <= baseline * 0.92 on average.
Rollout runbook validated: simulated failover, hard-rollback completed within SLA window in tabletop exercise.
Telemetry dashboard with acceptance histogram, per-model thresholds, false-accept/false-reject counters, and kernel-affinity mismatches is created and linked.
telemetry_and_metrics: Emit per-request: candidate_stack_id, kernel_fingerprint, prefill_probe_score, acceptance_score, prefill_probe_latency, decode_latency, committed_path (optimistic | slow), tokens_saved_estimate.
SLIs: acceptance_true_positive_rate, acceptance_false_positive_rate, p95_latency(opt), p95_latency(slow), cost_per_token_ratio
A/B experiment metrics: utility delta (QA metric), cost delta, latency delta, and per-model confidence drift over time.
Retention: raw acceptance traces stored 14 days; aggregates 90 days. Sensitive payloads redacted at emission point.
testing_plan: Unit tests for router decision logic including kernel affinity and KV cache compatibility checks.
Deterministic simulation harness that replays historical prefill+decode traces with injected kernel-level timing and toy models.
Performance tests: closed-loop 99th percentile under sustained load (5 minutes) at peak QPS seen in prod; run in perf lab against slow/fast stacks.
Chaos tests: force optimistic path failure, partial KV miss, and transport latency spikes to ensure fallback triggers within expected windows.
Online canary: internal tenant traffic for 72h, with automatic rollback if any SLO breach or acceptance drift > 5%.
Manual QA: small prompt corpus covering instruction-following, code generation, short/long context to validate quality preservation.
rollback_and_incident_playbook: Failure modes: acceptance metric skew (calibration bug), kernel-affinity break causing cache mismatch, regression in semantic quality, perf regressions at tail.
Immediate actions: toggle feature flag off for affected tenant(s). Perform soft-rollback first to route traffic to slow path incrementally.

Runbook steps: 1) collect last 1h traces, 2) compare acceptance distribution to baseline, 3) if kernel mismatch present escalate to infra, 4) if quality regression escalate to ModelOps and revert model variants.
Fallback policy: for transient infra blips prefer soft-commit with extended probation window; for quality regressions perform hard-rollback and mark router patch for hotfix release.
Post-incident: create postmortem within 72h with root cause, metrics, and corrective actions; adjust thresholds or disable auto-calibration as needed.
operational_notes: Auto-calibration is opt-in per-tenant; enterprise tenants receive a notification and can pin thresholds.
Kernel fingerprinting must be stable across runtime upgrades; add migration compatibility checks in CI.
Cache warming: when switching committed_path from optimistic -> slow, we should pre-seed KV cache where possible to reduce rollback cost.
Security: ensure probe payloads are sampled and scrubbed; do not log PII sequences in acceptance traces.
